Workloads that fit mostly in RAM may see little benefit, while frequent cache misses and IOPS limits make storage placement worth examining.

item.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI (22 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend that handles pushes to unrelated branches independently and reuses cached packfiles across fetches. It reduced median push latency by nearly 80% and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. The tradeoff is weaker consistency across branches and some redundant downloads, allowing writes to scale horizontally and reads to saturate clients' network connections.

item.title: Resisting Cognitive Surrender (12 minute read)
item.description: Uncritically accepting agent output can increase technical debt while eroding the understanding needed to debug and maintain a system. Choose how much to delegate based on risk, stay involved in consequential decisions, and ask for small, comprehensible changes. When delegating more fully, use independent observability, deterministic checks, and shadow traffic to verify behavior rather than relying solely on the agent's account.

item.title: Auditioning Engineering: Software Engineering Interviews in the Age of AI (6 minute read)
item.description: Warner Music Group encourages candidates to use AI while solving realistic API integration problems against a live, randomized test server. Its system-design interview asks candidates to modify an existing system and infer causes from observed behavior. The approach emphasizes technical judgment, although building new coding exercises and training senior system-design interviewers remain costly.

item.title: The weight-space programming post is misleading (5 minute read)
item.description: This critique separates experiments that inspect small networks' raw weights from larger-model experiments that use Python and execution feedback. The Qwen result involved 50 batches of practice problems, so it does not demonstrate improvement from inspecting raw weights alone. The distinction matters when judging whether the work shows one general capability or several different engineering techniques.

item.title: MCP and REST: How they fit together (Sponsor)
item.description: Your REST API already works. Learn what MCP adds for AI agents, how tool discovery works, and where each belongs in your architecture. When you're ready to build, WorkOS handles authentication for your MCP server.

item.title: djs (GitHub Repo)
item.description: djs is a JavaScript and TypeScript engine written in Rust for agent-generated scripts running in a WebAssembly sandbox. It keeps the entire VM state in one byte array, allowing execution to pause between instructions, snapshot while waiting for tools, and resume elsewhere. The focused runtime deliberately omits features such as ES modules, Intl, and a JIT.

item.title: Office Engine (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Office Engine embeds DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX viewing and editing in a browser through React or a web component. Progressive loading, Web Worker parsing, and virtualized views handle large files, while saves regenerate edited parts and preserve the original bytes elsewhere.

item.title: Three-Live (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Three-Live compiles a declarative subset of Three.js into GLB and USDZ assets for web, Android, and Apple rendering pipelines. It runs generated scripts with execution timeouts and geometry quotas, then hands the assets to platform-specific viewers. The Apache-licensed project is in Developer Preview and is not an officially supported Google product.

item.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (20 minute read)
item.description: Experiments show GPT-6 Astra reading and directly editing neural network weights without gradient descent, including writing small game-playing networks from scratch. Editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights reduced reasoning loops and raised MATH-500 accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% with 50 forward passes for feedback. The gains removed an obstacle to existing ability, while similar edits failed to meaningfully improve a Gemma model that rarely looped.

item.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996? (15 minute read)
item.description: A port of Stockfish running on a 200 MHz Pentium Pro with 64 MB of RAM reaches a measured rating of 3180 at 30 seconds per move. The experiment attributes much of chess engines' progress to better search and evaluation rather than faster hardware. Its roughly 3300 rating at classical time controls is extrapolated from shorter games, and readers can play the machine online.

item.title: HackerTV (Website)
item.description: HackerTV turns videos recommended in Hacker News comments into shared, continuously scheduled TV channels with a retro interface.

item.title: Mac at any scale (14 minute read)
item.description: Namespace explains the hardware, networking, virtualization, and VM-image distribution work behind running a fleet of Macs for cloud development and CI.

item.title: Curiosity Traps (7 minute read)
item.description: Subtle details, footnotes, and Easter eggs in public work can reward close attention and help people with shared interests find each other.

item.title: C++26 DIS failed, how does C++ survive? (7 minute read)
item.description: C++26's draft failed its ISO ballot amid objections to Contracts, leaving the committee to agree on a revised path and putting the release schedule in doubt.

item.title: A Pile of MCP Connectors Is Not A Context Engine (Sponsor)
item.description: Your team connected Slack, Jira and GitHub over MCP, and engineers still spend their time steering agents to the right answer. This article looks at why: connectors fetch from one tool at a time, so every agent stitches the pieces together itself, trusts the first doc that looks right, and adds a search to your token bill each time. Read what changes when a context engine sits on top of your connectors: the same coding task finished 83% faster at 48% lower cost.Read the blog post

item.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85% (18 minute read)
item.description: Cloudflare replaced full DNS zone rebuilds with a planner that selects the smallest provably safe update and a scheduler that combines work for the same zone. The changes cut peak memory by 85% and halved the delay from a DNS change to its data being written to Quicksilver without rebuilding tens of millions of records for a settings change.

item.title: Ship less JavaScript in Next.js with your AI agent (4 minute read)
item.description: Hidden import chains often load heavy code upfront that teams thought they had deferred, which slows page loads. Next.js 16.4 adds an agent skill that reads Turbopack's module graph, finds these problems, and can apply the fixes, plus new Bundle Analyzer views for route sizes, snapshot diffs, and the critical render path. At Vercel, it removed nearly 2 MB of compressed JavaScript across v0 and vercel.com, so Turbopack users can get similar savings with little manual work.

item.title: Porting 287,000 lines of React in 3 days. The hard part was proving nothing changed. (11 minute read)
item.description: Maple moved its observability app from React to Foldkit using about 40 Claude agents, with most human effort going into a harness that compared more than 2,600 screen variants across pixels, structure, network requests, and accessibility. The rewrite took three days, but code review still found about 180 defects the screenshots missed, and the startup bundle roughly doubled.

item.title: Hunger beats tenure: Advice for junior engineers (5 minute read)
item.description: Coding interviews no longer predict success when AI can outperform candidates on the same tasks, according to this hiring perspective. Newer engineers can stand out by tying their work to business goals, choosing one bold idea, and proving it with a weekend prototype.

item.title: Our organizations are being DDoSed from the inside (4 minute read)
item.description: AI makes it cheap to generate changes, but understanding, reviewing, and coordinating them still consumes the same limited human attention. Clearer intent about priorities and scope, plus a deliberate gate between experiments and the shared product, can help teams keep control of their direction.

item.title: Time to rethink software security because of AI? (10 minute read)
item.description: A single week brought a pile-up of major security failures: a certificate authority issued keys that were trivially guessable numbers, critical flaws hit PHP, GitLab, and Node.js, Railway leaked customer secrets, and PingCAP's TiDB control plane was breached for a month. AI now makes vulnerabilities faster to find and easier to exploit, even for nontechnical attackers. Teams will likely need automated patching, constant security monitoring, and AI-driven defense, and security will cost more.

item.title: Router.com: Choose the model that gets the job done without bankrupting you (Sponsor)
item.description: Each model call costs almost nothing... and then you get a $50K token bill. Router.com cuts your inference costs by matching every request to the most efficient model – balancing cost, speed, and quality of output. It's one endpoint with automatic fallbacks, request-level observability, and built-in privacy controls. Get your router.com API key

item.title: AiSOC (GitHub Repo)
item.description: AiSOC is a self-hostable security operations platform that combines alerts, uses LLM agents for triage, and supports investigations mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. A replayable decision ledger records agent steps, and an MCP server exposes the system to connected coding assistants.

item.title: Disc Image Studio (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Disc Image Studio turns images into data patterns that become visible artwork on the recording surface of CDs, DVDs, and single-layer Blu-ray discs. Windows supports design and burning, while experimental Linux and macOS command-line builds generate disc images offline.

item.title: CheerpJ 5.0 (10 minute read)
item.description: CheerpJ brings Java 21 and preview support for Java 25 to the browser, with a full OpenJDK that can compile as well as run Java applications. Its new WasmGC engine is experimental and opt-in, with production readiness planned for CheerpJ 6.0.

item.title: Doop (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Doop is a multiplayer design canvas where people and AI agents edit together through a built-in MCP server. It supports live cursors, threaded comments, clickable prototypes, and self-hosting with embedded Postgres for local development.

item.title: Warsaw in voxels (Website)
item.description: Explore central Warsaw as an interactive 3D voxel map built from GUGiK and OpenStreetMap data. Controls for date, time, and weather let you change the scene's lighting and atmosphere, and the source code is available to inspect.

item.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel? (8 minute read)
item.description: Ai2's benchmark, built from ICLR 2026 peer reviews, tests whether LLMs can judge research novelty and finds that small prompt changes can swing accuracy by more than 50 points on AI-generated ideas. Extra retrieval and reasoning did not reliably help, so teams using LLM judges should test their stability on the kinds of ideas they plan to score.

item.title: Automating agentic AI Well-Architected reviews with the AWS Agentic AI Lens (8 minute read)
item.description: Smarsh turned the AWS Agentic AI Lens into a Claude skill that checks all 150 best practices against a GitHub repository and produces an evidence-cited workbook in hours. The review surfaced gaps such as missing prompt-injection screening and cost controls, making follow-up architecture discussions more focused.

item.title: Reach 8 million tech professionals reading TLDR (Sponsor)
item.description: Ads get ignored on social media but not in TLDR! Reach software developers and engineering leaders where they actually pay attention. Learn more about sponsorship opportunities.

item.title: scriptc (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This experimental compiler turns TypeScript and JavaScript into native executables or WebAssembly.

item.title: ScanRuler (GitHub Repo)
item.description: ScanRuler measures 3D scans, compares them against CAD models, and maps wall thickness entirely in the browser.

item.title: October 2026 Express security releases (4 minute read)
item.description: The Express team patched denial-of-service flaws in body-parser and multer and recommends updating Node.js for the separate upstream Brotli decoder vulnerability.

item.title: Leaflet 2.0 beta (Website)
item.description: Leaflet's first 2.0 beta adds tree-shaking, bundled TypeScript types, and accessibility improvements, reducing a map with a tile layer from 38 kB to 25.6 kB gzipped while introducing breaking API changes.
